gaps.sentence: The match went ahead ___ the pouring rain.
gaps.explanation: Despite + noun phrase; 'although the rain' would need a clause (although it was raining).

gaps.sentence: Sales fell sharply last quarter; ___, the board cut the dividend.
gaps.explanation: The fall in sales caused the cut: as a result marks the consequence.

gaps.sentence: ___ the criticism, the festival has been renewed for three more years.
gaps.explanation: 'In spite of' + noun phrase concedes the criticism.

gaps.sentence: ___ most thrillers, the film reveals the killer in the opening scene.
gaps.explanation: 'Unlike + noun phrase' marks difference from a general category.

gaps.sentence: ___ the theory is elegant, the data simply don't support it.
gaps.explanation: 'Even though' grants the fact (the theory is elegant) before contradicting it.

gaps.sentence: Not only ___ the tickets cost more, but they sold out in minutes.
gaps.explanation: After fronted 'Not only', auxiliary inversion applies: Not only did the tickets cost more.

gaps.sentence: Take a jumper ___ the evening turns cold.
gaps.explanation: 'In case' = as a precaution against possibility.

gaps.sentence: The drug is remarkably effective. ___, it has almost no side effects.
gaps.explanation: 'Furthermore' introduces an additional point supporting the same claim.
